messages:
ana: quick heads-up — opened infra PR to tune autoscaling for the `jobs` namespace and add a new Karpenter provisioner profile. changes are: lower HPA min for batch jobs, add `provisioner = \"burstable-jobs\"`, set scaleDownDelaySeconds=300, and wire up a secret for metrics scraping. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234

ravi: thanks. one q — we run VPA on embeddings-service. does this touch embeddings or only jobs? worried about HPA/VPA collisions.

ana: it's jobs-only. embeddings lives in `apps/embeddings` and we didn't touch that folder. VPA policy is opt-in via label `autoscale/vpa: enabled` so no conflict here.

mike: quick nit — HPA should be autoscaling/v2 (v2beta2 is deprecated in our clusters). also ensure the `metrics` block is explicit. e.g.:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: batch-worker
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 65
```

sylvie: also note metrics-server needs access to the scrape token for our prometheus adapter (we use a small token injected as a secret into monitoring namespace). PR mentions a secret but the TF name should be `monitoring_metrics_token` not `metrics_token` to match other modules.

ci-bot: infra/pr-1234 — plan: SUCCESS. terraform plan: 6 to add, 2 to change, 1 to destroy. Logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/infra/1234

deploy-bot: preflight check failed on staging: `cluster-autoscaler` pod logs show errors resolving node label `karpenter.sh/provisioner-name`. -> RBAC problem for CA to list nodes?

ana: good catch — I missed a rolebinding in the TF module for autoscaler. pushed fix in the branch (rbac/allow-ca-listnodes). kek

mike: can we do a quick canary? suggest: spawn 30 concurrent jobs in `jobs` namespace to validate karpenter provisions new nodes and HPA scales pods. steps:
1) `kubectl -n jobs scale --replicas=30 deploy/batch-worker`
2) watch `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl get hpa -n jobs`
3) check node labels contain `karpenter.sh/provisioner-name=burstable-jobs`

sylvie: terraform snippet for secret wiring I used locally (works with our monitoring module):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_secret" "monitoring_metrics" {
  metadata {
    name      = "monitoring-metrics-token"
    namespace = "monitoring"
  }
  data = {
    token = base64encode(var.monitoring_metrics_token)
  }
}
```

ravi: about the RBAC — can you paste the rolebinding you added? want to review before we merge.

ana: sure — added this to `modules/cluster/rbac.tf`:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_role_binding" "ca_node_list" {
  metadata { name = "ca-node-list" namespace = "kube-system" }
  role_ref { api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" kind = "ClusterRole" name = "system:node-viewer" }
  subject { kind = "ServiceAccount" name = "cluster-autoscaler" namespace = "kube-system" }
}
```

ci-bot: infra/pr-1234 — apply queued (staging) after manual approval.

mike: one more ask — bump the provisioner `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` to a small value for this workload class so spot nodes drain quicker when idle. maybe 300?

ana: fine with 300, set in the provisioner profile as `ttlSecondsUntilExpired = 300` and `scaleDownDelaySeconds = 300`.

deploy-bot: staging apply completed: resources created: karpenter provisioner `burstable-jobs`, hpa batch-worker updated, monitoring secret applied.

ana: thanks all. I'll leave the PR open for 6h for any final objections then merge once overnight e2e is green. :thumbsup:
